item.title: Re: Thaumiel Factory Failure (seeking greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Thank you for your review. It is really insightful and helpful!

The first issue with this is that I have difficulty taking the Foundation response seriously. The researchers have no reason to believe that just because they found a location that produces anomalies, said anomalies will be automatically useful. It also makes me skeptical that they would immediately use said anomalies to assist the Foundation in the first place; the Foundation exists to contain anomalies first, not to put them to questionable/unreliable use. As a reader, I'm also confused as to how the researchers started running tests on the items in the first place, since the effects noted aren't really instinctive (for example, how would someone know which criteria to test to determine the specific effects of the box?).

That makes sense actually. The researchers wouldnt know anything about its anomalous effects so they probably wouldnt just throw other SCPs inside it and see what happens. They also wouldn't just use unreliable barely tested SCPs to contain others so it would never get classified as Thaumiel in the first place. I will try and figure something out to fix those issues!

…which brings me to the second major issue; I feel like there needs to be more explanation/worldbuilding behind why the warehouse behaves the way it does. I think we already have a Thaumiel location that knowingly assists the Foundation (I think it's a renovated schoolbuilding or the like; try using the Tag Search tool to find it), so what you have here just seems like a slight variation of it but without narrative context. Did the warehouse just spontaneously start existing to produce anomalies? Why does it want to help the Foundation at all?

I found the article in questions and yeah, they are kinda similar… What i could do to change that would be to make it non sapient and sentient and maybe not even a building… I just got a good idea of how to fix that! Will make another concept post.

Overall… I'm not convinced that this would be workable on the mainsite as currently presented. The Foundation personnel seem too quickly disappointed, and the warehouse itself seems shallowly developed. I think the first steps to take here would be to better develop the warehouse's history and motives so it exists as a meaningful character on its own, without needing the Foundation to give it significance.

Hmmm… Not too sure on how to addresse this problem. I need some time to think about a good backstory, but i get what you mean.

Thank you very much for your crit. It is really helpful!

item.title: Re: Thaumiel Factory Failure (seeking greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Got a PM about this, took a look.

The first issue with this is that I have difficulty taking the Foundation response seriously. The researchers have no reason to believe that just because they found a location that produces anomalies, said anomalies will be automatically useful. It also makes me skeptical that they would immediately use said anomalies to assist the Foundation in the first place; the Foundation exists to contain anomalies first, not to put them to questionable/unreliable use. As a reader, I'm also confused as to how the researchers started running tests on the items in the first place, since the effects noted aren't really instinctive (for example, how would someone know which criteria to test to determine the specific effects of the box?).

…which brings me to the second major issue; I feel like there needs to be more explanation/worldbuilding behind why the warehouse behaves the way it does. I think we already have a Thaumiel location that knowingly assists the Foundation (I think it's a renovated schoolbuilding or the like; try using the Tag Search tool to find it), so what you have here just seems like a slight variation of it but without narrative context. Did the warehouse just spontaneously start existing to produce anomalies? Why does it want to help the Foundation at all?

Also, last thing, note the difference between sentient and sapient. Sentience can be attributed to animals like dogs and cats and lobsters that can perceive and react to external stimuli and feel pain; sapience is what is needed for human-level self-awareness and communication ability.

Overall… I'm not convinced that this would be workable on the mainsite as currently presented. The Foundation personnel seem too quickly disappointed, and the warehouse itself seems shallowly developed. I think the first steps to take here would be to better develop the warehouse's history and motives so it exists as a meaningful character on its own, without needing the Foundation to give it significance.

item.title: Re: Thaumiel Factory Failure (seeking greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Thank you very much!

Okay, so what about it is those properties?

I was thinking about it being able to completely shield the exterior from harm caused by things inside the warehouse i.e. nuking the warehouse from the inside would not transmit the shockwave or heat to the outside. So you could for example put 079 in there and let someone look at a photograph of his but 079 would not be able to leave since he would cause harm to the world outside of the warehouse.

The problem with this warehouse being that anything from the outside can still cause harm to the warehouse and the inside of it especially. I was thinking along the lines that they wanted to make a small containment area inside of it, then began testing the durability of the walls and discovered that if you put a hole in the wall of this SCP from the outside, all organic matter inside the warehouse gets violently sucked through the hole making the warehouse not really useable for containment.

But if its thaumiel, how is this a waste of their time?

My idea was that it gets hastily classified as Thaumiel because the useful properties get discovered way before any of the over-the-top drawbacks get discovered making it not thaumiel but safe instead

This isn't entirely true. But it could be an interesting addition to the story. It may fall prey to the whole "Ending on a note" thing.

oh, good to know. i though all sentient SCPs are immediately Euclid since sentients is somewhat unpredictable. Also, i dont really know myself how i would make the note work soooo… Might leave it out, Might not. Will have to see how it looks when i m done writing it

thanks again!

item.title: Thaumiel Factory Failure (seeking greenlight) (will post revision due to glaring flaws)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Comedy, maybe some Emotional Aspects (only very few)

Elevator Pitch: A warehouse which has anomalous properties that could give it the thaumiel classification and which produces all kinds of objects that share that sentiment. They all have way too many drawbacks and weaknesses and are branded as failures by researchers (safe class instead of thaumiel) because of that.

Central Narrative:The warehouse gets discovered and testing ensues. At first the researchers are enthusiastic and hopeful of being able to find anomalies with which they might be able to contain really hazardous or hard to contain SCPs but get gradually more and more frustrated as their research shows what a waste of time this warehouse and its contents are. This is expressed through researcher notes and letters send to higher-ups, asking for reassignment to other SCPs.
I am also thinking about adding a small sad note that this SCP produces at the end, which explains that it just wants to help. This would however reclassify this anomaly as Euclid since it is sentient so i would leave that part out.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: So far, i personally haven't seen a thaumiel object that gets rebranded as safe (only ones that got neutralized) or an anomalous object which promises to be helpful but turns out useless in every way

Additional Notes: Some ideas of objects this SCP produces are:
-a cardboard box, which is able to lock anything inside of itself, but is way more flammable than normal cordboard, making it spontanously combust
-a pair of glasses which protects from visual cognitohazards but degrades eyesight until total blindness
-a hazmat suit which makes you immune to any disease while wearing it. After taking it off you are plagued by many lifelong alergies

No sandbox has been created at the time of posting.
English is not my first language, so please tell me if my grammar is terrible or my vacobulary sucks.
This is also my first SCP.
